subject.title: fix(mcp): allow token auth profiles for bearer projection

question: Should OpenClaw expose `mcp.servers.*.authProfileId` as the permanent generic core contract for binding a stored bearer-capable auth profile to an MCP server?
rationale: This is not only a mechanical fix: it adds a durable configuration field that decides which stored credential OpenClaw sends to remote MCP endpoints. The branch supplies a narrow implementation and compatibility alias, but choosing this public core surface requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept the neutral core selector
options.body: Adopt top-level `authProfileId` as the canonical MCP bearer binding and retain matching legacy OAuth-nested configuration as the documented compatibility path.

options.title: Keep service-specific credential binding outside core
options.body: Decline the generic selector and require the LifeOS-specific integration to own credential projection through an existing plugin or extension seam.

recommendation.title: Accept the neutral core selector
recommendation.body: Adopt top-level `authProfileId` as the canonical MCP bearer binding and retain matching legacy OAuth-nested configuration as the documented compatibility path.

likelyOwner.reason: Charles is the only supplied non-author signal tied to focused validation of this MCP auth-profile path; repository-history ownership could not be independently confirmed.
